title: Printable map extract with a 1 : 25 000 scale (lesson 62)
subject: Mathematics
unit: Summer 1: Enlargement and similarity; ratio and proportion; rates
source: Seeded from mathematics/y9 lesson 62 (Printable map extract with a 1 : 25 000 scale (portal worksheet for this lesson))
intro: Lesson 62: Ratio in context: maps, recipes and best value. To understand how to apply ratio to map scales, recipes and value-for-money decisions

blocks.text: Measure with a ruler to the nearest millimetre. On this map 1 cm stands for 25 000 cm = 250 m.

questions.q: Measure the masjid to the school on the map. How far is it in real life?
questions.a: 6 cm on the map: 6 × 25 000 = 150 000 cm = 1.5 km

questions.q: Measure the school to the farm along the road. How far is it in real life?
How far is it from the farm to the station?
A footpath is 2 km long. How long would it be on this map?
Map scale 1 : 50 000: how far is 8 cm on the map?
A recipe for 4 uses 150 g of lentils. How much for 10?
Better value: 6 eggs for £1.50 or 15 for £3.60?

(a) scale 1 : 20 000, map 7.5 cm: the real distance in km (b) real 2.4 km, scale 1 : 30 000: the map distance (c) a soup for 6 uses 900 ml of stock and 240 g of lentils: amounts for 15 (d) better value: 750 ml of olive oil for £5.25 or 1 litre for £6.80?
questions.a: (a) 1.5 km (b) 8 cm (c) 2250 ml and 600 g (d) 1 litre: 0.68p per ml against 0.7p per ml

questions.q: A recipe for 8 needs 3 eggs. How many eggs for 20 people?
Shop A sells dates at 400 g for £3.20. Shop B sells 1 kg for £7.50 with 10% off. Which is better value?
questions.a: A: £8 per kg; B: 7.50 × 0.9 = £6.75 per kg; Shop B

questions.q: On a 1 : 100 000 map, 1 cm stands for:
Big question: where do we use ratio without noticing?
questions.a: Reading maps, cooking for more people and choosing the best-value pack in a shop.
